t: Minimum Number of Valid Strings to Form Target II — Aho-Corasick + Jump Game
o: A 'valid' string is any non-empty prefix of any word, so forming `target` means tiling it with pieces, where a piece starting at index `i` may have any length from 1 up to `L[i]` — the longest prefix of some word that matches `target` starting at `i`. In Example 1, from index 0 the best piece is "aa" (prefix of "aaaaa"), giving the tiling "aa"+"bcd"+"abc" = 3 pieces. Example 2 shows one word can be reused, and Example 3 shows -1 when some character can't even start a piece. With sum of word lengths and target length up to 1e5, we need roughly linear time: precompute `L[i]` for every position efficiently (Aho-Corasick), then find the minimum number of pieces.
k: For each position i in target, only the maximum usable piece length L[i] matters; all shorter lengths 1..L[i] are also allowed.
Since every piece costs exactly 1, minimizing pieces is the classic Jump Game II problem on intervals [i+1, i+L[i]] — solvable greedily in O(n) without a segment tree.
Aho-Corasick over the words gives L[i] for all i in linear time: run target through the automaton and take the trie depth of the current state.

a.n: Approach 1: Brute-force DP with direct prefix matching
a.i: Let dp[i] be the minimum pieces to build target[0..i). From each reachable i, try every word and count how many characters match target starting at i; relax dp[i+len]. This directly mirrors the definition of a valid string and is easy to reason about, but checking every word at every position costs O(n · Σ|w|) in the worst case (~5e9), so it TLEs on large inputs — it serves as the conceptual baseline.
s: Initialize dp[0] = 0 and dp[i] = infinity otherwise.
For each i with dp[i] finite, for each word w, walk forward while w[k] == target[i+k] to get the match length len.
Relax dp[i+len] = min(dp[i+len], dp[i] + 1) for that len (any shorter prefix is also valid, but taking the max covers the interval).
Answer is dp[n], or -1 if unreachable.
a.t: O(n · Σ|w|) time — for each of the n positions we scan every word character by character; far too slow for the given limits.

a.i: Build an Aho-Corasick automaton of all words; each trie node's depth equals the length of the word-prefix it represents. Streaming target through the automaton yields, for each index i, the deepest matching state, hence L[i] = longest valid piece starting at i. Because every piece costs 1, choosing lengths reduces to Jump Game II: keep the farthest reachable index and count how many times we must extend the current piece boundary. This gives overall linear time.
s: Insert all words into a trie storing each node's depth; build failure links via BFS so the automaton can fall back to shorter prefixes.
Stream target through the automaton: at each character, follow fail links until a transition exists; the resulting node's depth is L[i].
Run the greedy: maintain curEnd (end of the current piece's coverage) and far (farthest index reachable so far); update far with i + L[i].
When i reaches curEnd, we must cut a new piece: increment the answer and set curEnd = far; if far <= i, return -1.
Return the answer if coverage reached n, else -1.
a.t: O(Σ|w| + n) time — building the trie and failure links is linear in total input size, streaming target through the automaton is amortized O(n) per character, and the greedy scan is O(n).
a.sp: O(Σ|w|) — the trie nodes plus failure/depth arrays.

w: In an interview, lead with the reduction: 'longest valid piece at each index' + 'minimum uniform-cost jumps', then implement Aho-Corasick for the first part and Jump Game II greed for the second. Common pitfalls: forgetting that all lengths 1..L[i] are valid (the greedy handles this automatically), mishandling the -1 case when a character matches no word prefix (automaton state falls back to the root with depth 0), and off-by-one errors on curEnd/far. An alternative to the greedy is dp with a segment tree supporting range-chmin updates, which also passes but is more code. Follow-ups might ask to reconstruct the actual pieces (store the chosen cut points during the greedy) or to handle streaming target queries.
